title: Keys API: don't gate cluster-wide access by a literal name/UID allowlist
answers: Why does list-keys refuse a legitimate service controller/access policy?
Cluster-wide list-keys returns 403 for a service credential that should be allowed
How should I gate an endpoint for 'service/system callers only'?
body:
Symptom: cluster-wide list-keys 403s for real service controllers across deployments/tenants.
Root cause: pkg/registry/apis/keys/handler.go previously checked identity.IsServiceIdentity plus a hardcoded UID/name allowlist; service credential names vary per deployment and per cluster in multi-tenant, so no literal list matches.
Fix pattern: replace name/UID matching with a type check, claims.IsIdentityType(info.GetIdentityType(), claims.TypeAccessPolicy), so any correctly-typed identity is admitted regardless of its name.
Constraints: use this when the real requirement is 'this caller is an access-policy/service identity', not 'this caller is one of N known names' — name allowlists break as soon as credentials are provisioned per workload/cluster.
applies: pkg/registry/apis/keys and any handler gating by caller identity rather than per-resource RBAC
says: Service credential blocked from listing encryption keys
List-keys returns 403 for legitimate service account
Access policy denied cluster-wide key list retrieval
Multi-tenant service account cannot access keys API
Why is valid service identity rejected by keys endpoint
search: The keys API handler requireClusterWideServiceCaller must authenticate cluster-wide service access using claims.IsIdentityType(info.GetIdentityType(), claims.TypeAccessPolicy) instead of name/UID allowlists, because service credential names vary per deployment and tenant in multi-tenant environments. Literal name/UID allowlists fail when credentials are provisioned per workload or cluster; the type check admits any correctly-typed access-policy identity regardless of name. Applies to pkg/registry/apis/keys/handler.go and any handler gating by caller identity type rather than per-resource RBAC.
